In the 14th century, a clock with a (37). to mark the hours was constructed; this is still in Salisbury Cathedral, England

- It was possibly built by druids (priests)

In the past, days were divided into 12 periods
- Shadow clocks have been discovered in {{33}} which consisted of a large column
- Some were constructed out of {{34}} and were several metres in height
Water clocks

- However, they were ineffective in {{35}} conditions. Engineers in China addressed this problem by using mercury and {{36}} of water instead.
